quorum.kill_rule: the brief fixed the ORDER of the attack — the ref the statuses are read at, then the SIGPIPE class across the whole of scripts/ rather than the one instance, then whether ten runs can distinguish a fix from luck — and each of those three produced a finding. Every refutation was re-run before it was acted on, and the one that does not reproduce is recorded as a lane error rather than dropped.
refuted_claims: That no pipeline in these scripts can return 141 — refuted 3/3 and right three times over: `git tag … | head -1` in dogfood_prev_tag, and `git tag … | grep -v … | head -1` in both tagged.sh and release-goal.sh. All three are one capture plus one awk or a parameter expansion now. The same grep found a NINETEENTH site this branch had just introduced (grep | head -1 | cut in the new status reader, one line from the defect being fixed), now one awk. Eighteen further sites elsewhere are filed as PMAT-240 with the census committed.

The ten-run loop as evidence — refuted 1/3: at one flake in three, ten passes have a 1.7% chance of being luck. Replaced by the_release_goal_scripts_carry_no_pipeline_that_can_take_sigpipe, which refuses the PATTERN in the three files this branch owns, ignores comments, and is red when one leaky pipeline is appended to any of them. The loop is kept as a weaker companion and the receipt no longer leans on it.

The red/green measurement, reported 'backwards' by two lanes — it does NOT reproduce. Re-run with main's two scripts checked out over this branch's tests: three cases fail (14 passed, 4 failed) and all pass at HEAD (18 passed), recorded in docs/audits/logs/PMAT-236-gate-tests.log. Two lanes agreeing is not a measurement.
lane_errors: Two of three lanes reported the red/green halves the wrong way round. The orchestrator re-ran both and recorded the result rather than taking the majority.
